newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila flour firms may re-enter U.S. market -trade.
newsitem.headline: Manila flour firms may re-enter U.S. market -trade.

text.p: Philippine flour companies may go back to the international grain market next week if wheat prices soften further in the United States, traders said on Friday.
"Some local millers were already looking for wheat requirements for late December and January 1997," said a trader at a U.S. commodity house.
The amount of wheat may reach at least 40,000 tonnes.
The Philippine grains market was quiet in the past week as buyers were sidelined due to high U.S. wheat prices.
One flour mill on Wednesday rejected bids for 16,000 tonnes of dark northern spring wheat and 8,000 tonnes of western white wheat for late December shipment.
"All the bids were high. They were selling at nearly US$200 a tonne C&F. We believe U.S. wheat is overpriced," a trader involved in the negotiations told Reuters.
Traders said they expected Philippine flour millers to book wheat requirements for January in the second half of December.
"But if prices fall to interesting levels next week, they might change their minds and buy earlier," a trader in a Japanese commodity house said.
Local flour prices were unchanged. The Trade and Industry Department said the price of a 25-kg bag of hard flour was unchanged at 290 pesos and soft flour was priced at 260 pesos.
Philippine corn importers may also start taking a look at the market following news Manila may buy between 250,000-300,000 tonnes of corn in the first quarter of 1997.
Agriculture Secretary Salvador Escudero told reporters on Wednesday he will ask President Fidel Ramos to approve the imports to head off a possible shortage of the staple next year.
The 150,000 tonnes of corn the government awarded at a tender last October has begun arriving in the Philippines.

On Wednesday, some 27,500 tonnes of corn aboard the MV Adrianopole arrived at the Asian Terminals Inc grains terminal in Bataan province north of Manila from the U.S. Pacific northwest. The corn was supplied by Continental Grain.
MV Keenung, carrying 27,500 tonnes of corn, was also scheduled to arrive on Saturday at the grain terminal in Mariveles.
MV Chian Mariner, with another cargo of 27,500 tonnes of corn from trader Glencore, will unload its cargo in Mariveles on December 1.
MV Sea Amuse, with a cargo of 25,000 tonnes from Japanese commodity house Kanematsu, was scheduled to deliver its shipment in Manila on December 7.
MV Pearl Sea, with another cargo of 27,500 tonnes of corn from Glencore, will arrive in Mariveles on December 11. The MV Sea Phoenix, with a cargo of 27,499 tonnes, will arrive on December 17.
"We expect 162,499 tonnes of imported corn in December because the suppliers were allowed to bring in 10 percent (above) the (government's) order," a government official said.

Local prices of corn were unchanged, with the retail price of yellow corn at 10.74 pesos a kg and white corn at 11.08 pesos per kg. Yellow corn was quoted at 6.51 pesos a kg and 6.41 pesos a kg for white corn.
US$1 = 26.20 pesos
